tools.description: Approve a PR / change. Optionally include a short review summary in the body field.

repo.description: Repository identifier — the provider's full name (for example 'owner/repo', 'group/subgroup/repo', or 'org/project/repo') or a full HTTPS / SSH URL. The bearer's workspace credential picks the right VCS installation automatically.

body.description: Optional review summary comment accompanying the approval.

repo.description: Repository identifier — the provider's full name (for example 'owner/repo', 'group/subgroup/repo', or 'org/project/repo') or a full HTTPS / SSH URL. The bearer's workspace credential picks the right VCS installation automatically.

path.description: Raw file path within the repo — do NOT URL-encode it (a literal %20 means a file whose name contains the characters %20).

ref.description: Optional ref: branch name, tag, or 7+ char SHA. Defaults to the repo's default branch HEAD.

limit_lines.description: Optional cap on lines returned. Default 500.

tools.name: litegit-find
tools.description: Glob the tree for matching paths (e.g. '**/*.py'). Useful for discovering the layout of a repo before reading specific files.

repo.description: Repository identifier — the provider's full name (for example 'owner/repo', 'group/subgroup/repo', or 'org/project/repo') or a full HTTPS / SSH URL. The bearer's workspace credential picks the right VCS installation automatically.

glob.description: Glob like '**/*.py' or 'src/**/test_*.ts', relative to root. Without max_depth, a literal file path returns that file; a literal directory lists files under it.

ref.description: Optional ref: branch name, tag, or 7+ char SHA. Defaults to the repo's default branch HEAD. The response reports the ref actually served (resolved_ref), its commit date, and when the mirror last synced (last_fetched_at) — check them before concluding something is absent, since an empty result on a stale tree is not proof it is missing.

refresh.description: Optional. Sync the repo mirror from origin before reading (default false). Costs a fetch, so leave it off for routine exploration; set it true when the answer depends on being current — above all before asserting something is absent, or when a prior read looked implausibly stale. Has no effect when ref is a SHA — a commit is immutable, so there is nothing newer to sync; use a branch name to get the latest. A large repo can take several minutes to sync and the call may time out before it finishes.

root.description: Optional subtree to scope to; default repo root.

max_depth.description: Optional maximum recursion depth relative to the caller's root (max 50).

tools.name: litegit-grep
tools.description: Search across the repo using POSIX ERE by default. Alternation, +, ?, (), and {} are supported; \d, (?i), lazy quantifiers, and lookaround are not. Use [0-9] for portable digits, regex='fixed' for literal strings, or regex='perl' for PCRE2 where available. Returns matching lines with file path + line number. Narrow with path_glob when possible — broad queries hit the upstream gateway's latency tail.

repo.description: Repository identifier — the provider's full name (for example 'owner/repo', 'group/subgroup/repo', or 'org/project/repo') or a full HTTPS / SSH URL. The bearer's workspace credential picks the right VCS installation automatically.

pattern.description: Pattern to search for. The default POSIX ERE mode supports alternation, +, ?, (), and {}; it does not support \d, (?i), lazy quantifiers, or lookaround. Use [0-9] for portable digits, regex='fixed' for literal strings, or regex='perl' for PCRE2 where available.

regex.description: Pattern dialect. 'extended' (default) = POSIX ERE. 'fixed' = literal string, no metacharacters. 'basic' = POSIX BRE, where | + ? ( ) { } match literally unless backslash-escaped. 'perl' = PCRE2, adding \d, (?i), lazy quantifiers and lookaround where the server supports it.

limit_lines.description: Lines per page. Default and maximum: 2000. Larger values fail with MT-VALIDATION. Pass a non-null next_start_line as start_line to read the next page. The runtime byte limit may shorten a page further.

tools.name: litegit-search-issues
tools.description: Cross-repo issue search using GitHub's /search/issues syntax. Scope with 'org:qodo-ai' / 'repo:owner/name' qualifiers — bare queries hit public GitHub globally.

query.description: GitHub /search/issues syntax. Scope with qualifiers — 'org:qodo-ai foo' or 'repo:owner/name state:open'. Without an org: / repo: qualifier the search is global across public GitHub.

tools.name: litegit-search-repos
tools.description: List or search the repositories your key can access (across all providers). Call with NO query to list your repos (up to max_results, default 200); pass a substring query to filter by repo full_name (e.g. query="litegit" -> qodo-ai/litegit-gateway). Use this FIRST to find which repo a file or path lives in, or to enumerate accessible repos — do not guess repo names. Returns {repos, truncated, next_page_token}; if truncated is true the cap was hit — narrow with a query or raise max_results to see the rest.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter on a repo's full_name (owner/repo). Omit to list ALL accessible repos; pass e.g. 'litegit' to match 'qodo-ai/litegit-gateway'. This is a plain substring, not a glob or regex.

provider.description: Optional VCS provider filter (e.g. 'github', 'gitlab', 'bitbucket'). Omit to span every provider the bearer can reach.

max_results.description: Optional cap on repos returned. Default 200.

tools.name: litegit-set-labels

repo.description: Repository identifier — the provider's full name (for example 'owner/repo', 'group/subgroup/repo', or 'org/project/repo') or a full HTTPS / SSH URL. The bearer's workspace credential picks the right VCS installation automatically.

labels.description: Label names to set. Replaces the full label set (not additive).

tools.description: Update the title and/or description body of a PR / change. Omit either field to leave it unchanged.

repo.description: Repository identifier — the provider's full name (for example 'owner/repo', 'group/subgroup/repo', or 'org/project/repo') or a full HTTPS / SSH URL. The bearer's workspace credential picks the right VCS installation automatically.

title.description: New PR title. Omit to leave unchanged.

body.description: New PR description body (markdown). Omit to leave unchanged.

tools.name: cross-repo-overview
tools.description: Return the whole workspace's cross-repo relation graph: the participating repos (nodes) and the relations between them (edges) in one call. Optional filters narrow by provider, git organization, or status. Use this to map how repos across the workspace relate, rather than querying one repo at a time. Large workspaces are capped — when 'truncated' is true the view is partial; narrow with the filters to see the rest.

provider.description: Optional. Restrict to repos on these providers (github / gitlab / ado / bitbucket).

git_organization.description: Optional. Restrict to repos under these orgs / groups / workspaces.

status.description: Optional. Subset of pending|completed|failed|not_found. Omitted -> all statuses.

tools.name: cross-repo-pair
tools.description: Explain the single cross-repo relation between TWO specific repositories: the relation type, a one-liner, and the full narrative of how they relate and what changes in either can affect the other. Call with two 'owner/repo' full names (order does not matter — the relation is undirected). Use this when you already know both repos and want the detailed connection between them, rather than listing one repo's whole blast radius. Errors if the two repos have no analyzed relation.

repo.description: One provider-native repo full name. Order does not matter.

related_repo.description: The other provider-native repo full name.

repo_provider.description: Optional VCS provider (github / gitlab / ado / bitbucket) for 'repo', when that owner/repo exists on more than one.

related_repo_provider.description: Optional VCS provider for 'related_repo', when it exists on more than one.

tools.name: cross-repo-relations
tools.description: List the cross-repo relations for ONE repository: every other repo it is coupled to, with the relation type, a one-liner, and a longer narrative of how they relate and what changes in either can affect the other. Call with a 'owner/repo' full name. Returns edges of every status — pending (analysis still running), completed, failed, and not_found (checked, no coupling). Use this to understand a single repo's blast radius. Pass shallow=true to skip the narrative when you only need the list of coupled repos; for one specific pair's full explanation use cross-repo-pair.

repo.description: Provider-native repo full name, including nested group/project segments.

provider.description: Optional VCS provider (github / gitlab / ado / bitbucket) when the same owner/repo exists on more than one.

shallow.description: Optional, default false. When true, return only the connection skeleton (related repo, status, relation type, one-liner) and omit the longer 'relationship' narrative — cheaper when you just need to list which repos this one is coupled to. Set false (or omit) to get the full narrative; for one specific pair's full explanation use cross-repo-pair.

tools.name: get-pr-review-findings
tools.description: Get the current review state of ONE pull/merge request from Qodo's review DB: the latest review run (status + reviewed commit) and every current finding with its id, status, category, action level, and the run + commit that raised it. Structured and git-provider-agnostic — use this instead of reading the PR's review comments to check where a review stands or which findings are still open. Call with the full HTTP(S) PR URL, not a repo slug or PR number. Returns review_session=null when the PR has no recorded review yet.Set extended=true for programmatic audit or investigation: includes finding locations, code snippets, dismissal details, evidence with citations, and review-run history. Default false returns the compact review state. This reads stored results, not a new review or an immutable history of every finding revision. Evidence may be null. If qar_operation_result_truncated=true is returned, the result exceeded the size limit and is not a complete review read.attribution_status is one of: pending, partial_implementation, not_implemented, focus_areas_edited, full_implementation, dismissed, detected_after_merge, outdated. OPEN (still needs attention) = pending, partial_implementation, not_implemented, focus_areas_edited. CLOSED = full_implementation, dismissed, detected_after_merge, outdated. action_level is severity, NOT open-vs-closed.Use the returned finding ids with pr-review-dismiss or pr-review-mark-implemented to close findings out.

pr_url.description: Full http:// or https:// URL of the pull/merge request, including its hostname; for example, https://github.com/org/repo/pull/123. A repo slug or PR number is not a URL.

extended.description: Return extended review details: finding locations and code snippets, dismissal details, stored evidence (explanation and citations), and review-run history. Default false keeps the compact response. Reads stored results; does not rerun or deepen the review. Evidence is null when unavailable.

git_provider.description: Deprecated compatibility-only input. It is ignored; identify the pull/merge request with pr_url and omit this argument in new callers.

tools.name: pr-review-dismiss
tools.description: Dismiss one or more local or PR review findings with a reason — closing them WITHOUT a code change, because they are wrong, intentional, out of scope, or declined. Updates the findings in Qodo's review DB, strikes through their PR comments, re-renders the review summary. A local dismissal preserves configured merge-policy blocks. Use pr-review-mark-implemented instead when you actually fixed the code. Only OPEN findings can be dismissed; ids that are already closed come back with their own per-finding outcome rather than failing the call. Get the ids from get-pr-review-findings.

finding_ids.description: Finding UUIDs to update, as returned in each finding's `id` by get-pr-review-findings. 1-100 per call. Batch every finding on the same PR into ONE call: the PR-side reconciliation runs once per call, not once per finding.

local_review_id.description: For local findings, the local_review_id returned by that review. Required to prevent acting on a stale result. Batch only findings from that local review.

reason.description: Why the findings are being closed without a code change. false_positive: the finding is wrong. intentional: the code is deliberate and correct as written. deferred: real, but out of scope for this PR. rejected: understood and declined.

explanation.description: Short justification recorded alongside the dismissal and shown to reviewers. Strongly recommended. Max 2000 characters.

tools.name: pr-review-mark-implemented
tools.description: Mark one or more PR review findings as implemented — the fix HAS landed in the code. Updates the findings in Qodo's review DB, marks their PR comments resolved, re-renders the review summary, and clears the merge-policy block they were holding. Only claim this for findings you actually fixed: it clears the merge gate without a review having verified the fix. Use pr-review-dismiss when closing a finding without a code change. Only OPEN findings can be marked; ids that are already closed come back with their own per-finding outcome rather than failing the call. Get the ids from get-pr-review-findings.

finding_ids.description: Finding UUIDs to update, as returned in each finding's `id` by get-pr-review-findings. 1-100 per call. Batch every finding on the same PR into ONE call: the PR-side reconciliation runs once per call, not once per finding.

local_review_id.description: For local findings, the local_review_id returned by that review. Required to prevent acting on a stale result. Batch only findings from that local review.

explanation.description: Short note on what was changed to fix the findings. Strongly recommended. Max 2000 characters.

tools.name: pull-request-by-file

Call with 'owner/repo', the git provider, and the exact current default-branch file path (PRs that touched it before a rename are included). Use this to see the change history of a file across PRs.

repo.description: Provider-native repository full name, including nested group/project segments.

provider.description: Optional. Git provider override; resolved automatically from the repo when omitted (github / gitlab / bitbucket / ado).

file_path.description: Exact current default-branch file path; PRs that touched it (pre-rename) are returned.

sort_direction.description: Optional. Sort by merge time ascending or descending (default desc).

include_file_changes.description: Optional. Include each returned PR's file changes (default false).

tools.name: pull-request-details

repo.description: Provider-native repository full name, including nested group/project segments.

provider.description: Optional. Git provider override; resolved automatically from the repo when omitted (github / gitlab / bitbucket / ado).

tools.name: pull-request-patch
tools.description: Fetch the diff/patch for ONE file within ONE merged pull request. Call with 'owner/repo', the git provider, the PR number, and the exact file path. Use this to read exactly what a PR changed in a given file.

repo.description: Provider-native repository full name, including nested group/project segments.

provider.description: Optional. Git provider override; resolved automatically from the repo when omitted (github / gitlab / bitbucket / ado).

file_path.description: Exact file path within the PR to retrieve the patch for.

tools.name: pull-request-review-history
tools.description: Get the recent code-review fix suggestions for a file or directory in ONE repository — what reviewers flagged there in past PRs and whether each suggestion was accepted. Call with 'owner/repo' and a relative path; the search graduates up the directory tree until enough suggestions are found. Use this to learn what kinds of issues recur in an area of the code and what feedback the team accepts.

repo.description: Provider-native repository full name, including nested group/project segments.

provider.description: Optional. Git provider override; resolved automatically from the repo when omitted (github / gitlab / bitbucket / ado).

file_path.description: Relative path to a file or directory. The search starts here and graduates up the directory tree until enough suggestions are found.

limit.description: Optional max number of suggestions to return (1-100, default 20).

acceptance_status.description: Optional. Filter suggestions by review outcome; all outcomes are included when omitted.

category.description: Optional. Filter by finding category: 'bug' for bug findings, 'rule' for convention/style.

include_code_hunks.description: Optional. Include the diff hunk for each suggestion location, for pattern matching against the current code (default false).

tools.name: pull-request-similar
tools.description: Find merged pull requests semantically similar to a query for ONE repository — past changes that touched the same area or solved a comparable problem. Call with 'owner/repo', the git provider, and a query describing the change/issue/code element. Optionally narrow by a file path prefix. Use this to learn how similar work was done before.

repo.description: Provider-native repository full name, including nested group/project segments.

provider.description: Optional. Git provider override; resolved automatically from the repo when omitted (github / gitlab / bitbucket / ado).

query.description: Search string describing the change / issue / code element to find similar merged PRs for.

file_path_prefix.description: Optional path prefix to limit the search to a subdirectory or a specific file.

similarity_top_k.description: Optional max number of similar PRs to return (1-50, default 10).

include_file_changes.description: Optional. Include each returned PR's file changes (default false).

tools.name: pull-request-similar-suggestions
tools.description: Semantically search the code-review fix suggestions of ONE repository — find past findings similar to a description (embed_type 'description') or given on similar code (embed_type 'diff_hunk'). Call with 'owner/repo' and a query; optionally filter by folder, category (bug / rule), or acceptance status. Use this to check whether a finding was raised before and how the team responded.

repo.description: Provider-native repository full name, including nested group/project segments.

provider.description: Optional. Git provider override; resolved automatically from the repo when omitted (github / gitlab / bitbucket / ado).

query.description: Text to embed and search against — a finding description or a code snippet.

embed_type.description: Optional. What to match against: 'description' compares to suggestion description text, 'diff_hunk' compares to the code diff hunks at suggestion locations (default 'description').

folder_path.description: Optional folder prefix; only suggestions whose affected file path starts with it are returned.

category.description: Optional. Filter by finding category: 'bug' for bug findings, 'rule' for convention/style.

acceptance_status.description: Optional. Filter suggestions by review outcome; all outcomes are included when omitted.

top_k.description: Optional max number of unique suggestions to return (1-100, default 50).

include_code_hunks.description: Optional. Include the diff hunk for each suggestion location, for pattern matching against the current code (default false).

tools.name: pull-request-stats
tools.description: Summarize the indexed PR-knowledge corpus for ONE repository: counts of merged PRs, file changes, patches, comments, fix suggestions, and the merge-date range. Call with 'owner/repo' and the git provider. Use this to gauge how much PR history is available before deeper queries.

repo.description: Provider-native repository full name, including nested group/project segments.

provider.description: Optional. Git provider override; resolved automatically from the repo when omitted (github / gitlab / bitbucket / ado).

tools.name: review-notes-bind-pr
tools.description: After opening a PR, associate active published PR Review Notes using notes_id and positive pr_number. Target repository comes from the saved notes. Retries of the same association are idempotent; conflicting associations return a conflict. No content edit, revision, SHA recapture or provider verification occurs. Returns a bounded receipt with IDs, revisions and a document summary; use read tools for full content.

tools.name: review-notes-find-tracks
tools.description: Call at task intake or when continuing an existing development effort. Find published Development Track Notes by canonical Linear/Jira identity, registered repository identity, title and status. Returns candidates and nextCursor; follow after for subsequent candidates. Each collection page contains at most one full record even when limit is higher; select a track explicitly. Repository overlap never proves membership. No SQL or prose lookup. Results over the notes response budget return result_is_page=true, JSON text, record revisions, result_digest and next_read_cursor. Repeat the exact original arguments plus read_cursor until next_read_cursor is null; concatenate text without separators and parse JSON once before editing. Inline agents receive smaller pages bounded by their model's compaction caps; editable documents are exact copies. Do not save a partial reconstruction. MT-CONFLICT means the snapshot changed: discard pages and restart.

tools.name: review-notes-for-pr
tools.description: Read both published PR Review Notes and their explicitly linked Development Track Notes for a bound PR. Supply the target repository identity, PR number and actual current PR HEAD, obtained through LiteGit. Returns lookup_status, both records, revision/provenance, validation applicability and effective digest. Does not bind pre-PR notes; storage/access errors are errors, never no_pr_notes. No reviewer delegation. Results over the notes response budget return result_is_page=true, JSON text, record revisions, result_digest and next_read_cursor. Repeat the exact original arguments plus read_cursor until next_read_cursor is null; concatenate text without separators and parse JSON once before editing. Inline agents receive smaller pages bounded by their model's compaction caps; editable documents are exact copies. Do not save a partial reconstruction. MT-CONFLICT means the snapshot changed: discard pages and restart.

tools.name: review-notes-get-pr
tools.description: Read PR Review Notes by notes_id, or by complete provider/provider_host/target_repo_ref/pr_number. A PR number alone is ambiguous. Default reads published notes; draft=true requests the latest saved draft for editing. Returns the explicit track_id; get-track reads that track. Does not create an association. Results over the notes response budget return result_is_page=true, JSON text, record revisions, result_digest and next_read_cursor. Repeat the exact original arguments plus read_cursor until next_read_cursor is null; concatenate text without separators and parse JSON once before editing. Inline agents receive smaller pages bounded by their model's compaction caps; editable documents are exact copies. Do not save a partial reconstruction. MT-CONFLICT means the snapshot changed: discard pages and restart.

tools.name: review-notes-get-track
tools.description: Read Development Track Notes by track_id. Default is the published document; draft=true reads the latest saved draft before editing. Returns IDs, latest/published revisions and provenance. include_prs=true also returns one connected PR record and linkedPrs.nextCursor, not its code. Follow that cursor with prs_after and include_prs=true for subsequent connected PRs. Results over the notes response budget return result_is_page=true, JSON text, record revisions, result_digest and next_read_cursor. Repeat the exact original arguments plus read_cursor until next_read_cursor is null; concatenate text without separators and parse JSON once before editing. Inline agents receive smaller pages bounded by their model's compaction caps; editable documents are exact copies. Do not save a partial reconstruction. MT-CONFLICT means the snapshot changed: discard pages and restart.

tools.name: review-notes-history
tools.description: Read an authorized bounded page of immutable track or PR notes revisions. scope selects track or pr; record_id selects its UUID. Each collection page returns at most one full revision; follow next_before using before, independently of content read_cursor. limit is an upper bound. Includes drafts. Historical repository authorization is enforced by the platform. Results over the notes response budget return result_is_page=true, JSON text, record revisions, result_digest and next_read_cursor. Repeat the exact original arguments plus read_cursor until next_read_cursor is null; concatenate text without separators and parse JSON once before editing. Inline agents receive smaller pages bounded by their model's compaction caps; editable documents are exact copies. Do not save a partial reconstruction. MT-CONFLICT means the snapshot changed: discard pages and restart.

tools.name: review-notes-prepare-pr
tools.description: Call before PR creation with final existing source HEAD, PR Review Notes and explicit track selection. Saves and publishes notes atomically and returns ready_to_open_pr only after the platform acknowledges durable publication. Uses the save-pr fields, with publish always true. No marker commit, push or PR write. If HEAD changes before opening, refresh and republish the notes first. MCP callers capture Git identity in their workspace; CLI captures locally. After opening, bind-pr with the returned notes ID and PR number. Returns a bounded receipt with IDs, revisions and a document summary; use read tools for full content.

tools.name: review-notes-publish-pr
tools.description: Publish the latest saved PR notes revision. Uses its captured commit SHA without recapturing HEAD or changing content. Returns a durable receipt. Use prepare-pr to save and publish refreshed notes together. Returns a bounded receipt with IDs, revisions and a document summary; use read tools for full content.

tools.name: review-notes-publish-track
tools.description: Publish one saved latest Development Track revision using record_id and revision. Saving a draft does not change reviewers' input. Returns the durable publication receipt; does not schedule a review itself. Returns a bounded receipt with IDs, revisions and a document summary; use read tools for full content.

tools.name: review-notes-resolve-repository
tools.description: Resolve an exact provider repository path and hostname to its registered canonical notes identity. repo_ref is an opaque ID, not owner/repo. Uses the authenticated platform registry and makes no Git provider request. Missing, inactive or ambiguous matches fail explicitly. Resolve both source and target repositories when preparing notes for a fork. Optional bounded repo_candidates disambiguate local remote URL forms using a unique exact registered path; always include the primary repo.

tools.name: review-notes-save-pr
tools.description: Create or edit PR Review Notes: Intent, Decision, Review focus, Validation and Known gap. Supply a full document and explicitly select track_id or no_track_reason. commit_sha_at_update is the existing source HEAD captured for this save. Creation records that SHA in both commit fields; edits preserve the original creation SHA. Supply notes_id and latest expected_revision when editing, or creation_key and revision=0 when creating. Optional positive pr_number asserts association in the saved target repository; initial association requires active published notes. publish=false is a draft; publish=true is atomic publication. This tool neither verifies a PR remotely nor writes Git. Local CLI captures Git; MCP callers supply it. Returns a bounded receipt with IDs, revisions and a document summary; use read tools for full content.

tools.name: review-notes-save-track
tools.description: Create or edit Development Track Notes for overall intent, product decisions, business impact, connected repos/PRs and merge/release order. Supply the full document; preserve unrelated existing notes. On creation, omit track_id, set expected_revision=0 and retain creation_key for retries. On edit use track_id and the latest_revision from a draft read. publish=false saves a private draft; publish=true publishes atomically. Read grants suffice; platform checks every referenced repository. A conflict requires rereading and merging. Returns a bounded receipt with IDs, revisions and a document summary; use read tools for full content.

tools.name: review-skills-bulk
tools.description: Apply one operation to many skills by id in a single call: activate, deactivate, enable_steering, disable_steering, or set_scope (with scopes or scope_elements). Best-effort, not all-or-nothing — check the returned matched/succeeded counts and per-id failures rather than assuming every id changed. set_scope CASCADES to every rule linked to each selected skill (their scopes are overwritten to match). Requires Review Standards edit permission. Confirm with the user before calling; set dry_run=true first to preview how many skills would change.

operation.description: activate / deactivate: set state. enable_steering / disable_steering: set application mode. set_scope: replace scopes (requires scopes or scope_elements, never both).

skill_ids.description: Id(s) of the skills to change (id from review-skills-list/review-skills-get) — a single integer or a non-empty array of integers. At least one.

scopes.description: The NEW full list of scope paths for the skill/skills (replaces the current list, no merge) — a single path or an array, e.g. '/owner/repo/' or '/owner/repo/modules/<name>/'. An empty list means the universal scope '/'. WARNING: every rule linked to a skill has its scopes overwritten to mirror the skill's new scopes — the skill is the scope source of truth for its linked rules. The platform enforces its configured scope limit.

scope_elements.description: The NEW full scope list, using platform scope elements, instead of scopes. Example: [{"kind":"repo","repo":{"fullName":"owner/repo"},"path":"src"}]. Use kind=org with org, or kind=global for universal scope. Empty list also means universal. Historical blank/* identities are accepted; check their returned flat scopes for actual reach. Prefer kind=global for new universal assignments. The platform enforces its configured scope limit. Replaces the current list and CASCADES to every linked rule. Supply either scope_elements or scopes, never both.

dry_run.description: Preview only: report how many skills would change without changing anything. Default false.

tools.name: review-skills-discover
tools.description: Start standards discovery for explicit registered repository_ids. This MUTATES workspace standards: both repository rules and skills may be extracted and persisted; it is not a skills-only scan. Requires Review Standards edit permission, the platform feature and manual-discovery eligibility. No dry run. Running repositories continue their existing runs; selecting completed/failed repositories requests re-extraction/retry. Optional rules_prompt/skills_prompt customize extraction and must be approved. Returns workspace-wide status, not a per-request completion receipt. Retain the selection, poll status with a bound, then verify source records. After a timeout inspect status/records, never blindly start again.

repository_ids.description: Explicit registered repository ids from source-repositories; never provider ids or names.

tools.name: review-skills-discovery-status
tools.description: Read workspace-wide standards discovery eligibility, progress, rules/skills totals and per-repository failures without starting work. Requires Review Standards edit permission and the platform discovery feature. isEligible=false means manual discovery is unavailable under current automatic-import settings. Counts include other repository runs; availableRepositoryIds lists never-started repositories only, not every repository that may be selected. Verify selected sources with review-skills-list/get.

tools.name: review-skills-get
tools.description: Fetch one skill by id, including its repo, path, scopes, scopeElements, applicationMode, state, and (with include_insights) per-skill usage metrics. Use before editing a skill to show the user its current form.

skill_id.description: Id of the skill to fetch (id from review-skills-list).

tools.name: review-skills-insights
tools.description: Workspace-wide skills metrics (invoked / findings_produced / merged_unresolved) aggregated over a fixed 30-day window. No parameters.

tools.name: review-skills-list
tools.description: List skills discovered in the workspace's repositories, with filters and pagination (returns items/total/page/size/pages). Skills are discovered from repos, not authored — there is no create/delete tool. Use repo_scope / name_contains / is_relevant / state / application_mode / scopes to narrow, include_insights to attach per-skill usage metrics. An empty page is a valid result.

repo_scope.description: Filter to skills discovered in exactly this repository, e.g. 'owner/repo'.

is_relevant.description: Filter by relevance status (whether the extraction judged the skill worth keeping).

state.description: Filter by lifecycle state. Omit for both states.

application_mode.description: rules: apply extracted rules. steering: make the skill available to the review agent, which decides whether to consult it. Availability does not guarantee invocation.

scopes.description: Filter by application scope paths, e.g. '/owner/target-repo/'. Includes ancestor scopes by platform default. repo_scope instead filters the skill's source repository.

include_insights.description: Attach per-skill insights (invoked / findings_produced / merged_unresolved) to each result.

tools.name: review-skills-source-repositories
tools.description: Find registered source repositories by name/provider, with items/total/page/pageSize pagination. Returns id/fullName/provider/htmlUrl and connection metadata, not credentials. Search is partial: resolve an exact path and host before selecting ids; traverse matching pages. An empty result does not grant repository access; use the existing provider connection flow.

tools.name: review-skills-update
tools.description: Update a skill's state, application_mode, and/or scopes (at least one required). Use scopes or scope_elements for scope replacement, never both. WARNING: changing scopes CASCADES to every rule linked to this skill — the skill is the scope source of truth for its linked rules, so their scopes are overwritten to match. Confirm the exact change with the user, and tell them about the cascade, before calling. Requires Review Standards edit permission. Returns the updated skill.

skill_id.description: Id of the skill to update (id from review-skills-list/review-skills-get).

scopes.description: The NEW full list of scope paths for the skill/skills (replaces the current list, no merge) — a single path or an array, e.g. '/owner/repo/' or '/owner/repo/modules/<name>/'. An empty list means the universal scope '/'. WARNING: every rule linked to a skill has its scopes overwritten to mirror the skill's new scopes — the skill is the scope source of truth for its linked rules. The platform enforces its configured scope limit.

scope_elements.description: The NEW full scope list, using platform scope elements, instead of scopes. Example: [{"kind":"repo","repo":{"fullName":"owner/repo"},"path":"src"}]. Use kind=org with org, or kind=global for universal scope. Empty list also means universal. Historical blank/* identities are accepted; check their returned flat scopes for actual reach. Prefer kind=global for new universal assignments. The platform enforces its configured scope limit. Replaces the current list and CASCADES to every linked rule. Supply either scope_elements or scopes, never both.

application_mode.description: rules: apply extracted rules. steering: make the skill available to the review agent, which decides whether to consult it. Availability does not guarantee invocation.

tools.name: rules-bulk
tools.description: Apply one operation to many rules by id in a single atomic call: activate, deactivate, set_scope (with the scopes argument), accept_activate (approve pending suggestions), or reject. reject PERMANENTLY DELETES pending suggestions and cannot be undone — always dry_run first, show the user the affected count, and get explicit confirmation. Requires admin permission. Returns matched/succeeded counts plus per-id failures.

operation.description: activate / deactivate: set state. set_scope: replace scopes (requires the scopes argument). accept_activate: approve pending suggestions into active rules. reject: PERMANENTLY DELETE pending suggestions (irreversible).

rule_ids.description: Id(s) of the rules to change (ruleId from search/list) — a single integer or a non-empty array of integers. At least one.

scopes.description: Only with operation=set_scope: the new full scopes list (empty = universal '/').

dry_run.description: Preview only: report how many rules would change without changing anything. Default false.

tools.name: rules-create
tools.description: Create a new coding rule in the workspace. Confirm the exact rule (name, severity, content, scopes) with the user before calling. Admin callers create the rule active immediately; non-admin callers create a PENDING suggestion an admin must approve — check the returned state and tell the user which happened. A duplicate name is rejected; pick a different name rather than retrying. Returns the full created rule (ruleId, state, and every other field).

name.description: Concise unique rule name (max 128 chars). Duplicates are rejected.

category.description: Rule category, e.g. Security, Correctness, Quality, Reliability, Performance, Testability, Compliance, Accessibility, Observability, Architecture.

severity.description: error = must comply; warning = comply by default; recommendation = apply when appropriate.

content.description: What the rule checks or enforces, 1-3 sentences, imperative voice.

good_examples.description: Code snippet(s) that FOLLOW the rule. Pass '' only when no example makes sense.

bad_examples.description: Code snippet(s) that VIOLATE the rule. Pass '' only when no example makes sense.

scopes.description: Repository scope paths the rule applies to, e.g. '/owner/repo/' or '/owner/repo/src/module/'. Max 25. Omit for the universal scope '/'.

tools.name: rules-get
tools.description: Fetch one rule by id, including content, examples, scopes, state, and severity. Use before editing a rule to show the user its current form.

rule_id.description: Id of the rule to fetch (ruleId from search/list).

tools.name: rules-list
tools.description: List the workspace's coding rules with filters and pagination (page/totalCount/rules). Use state='pending' to list suggestions awaiting triage, scopes to narrow to a repository, categories/severity/name_contains to filter further. Prefer rules-search for 'which rules apply to this task'; use rules-list for browsing, triage, and finding rule ids to manage. Rules auto-derived from skills never appear here — they are managed through their skill, not the rules tools. An empty page is a valid result.

state.description: Filter by lifecycle state: 'pending' (suggestions awaiting triage), 'active', 'inactive', or a comma-separated combination. Omit for all states.

categories.description: Filter to rules whose category is any of these (see rules-metadata for values).

scopes.description: Filter to rules applicable at these scope paths, e.g. '/owner/repo/'.

tools.name: rules-metadata
tools.description: The workspace's rule metadata: available categories, severities, and source types. Call before creating a rule so the category matches an existing one.

tools.name: rules-search
tools.description: Search the workspace's coding rules for those most relevant to a coding task, ranked by semantic relevance. Call BEFORE writing, editing, refactoring, or reviewing code so the returned rules can be applied to the change. Pass a structured Name/Category/Content query describing the rule the task would trigger (see the query parameter for the exact format); optionally narrow to a repository scope. For best coverage call twice — once with a topic query for the task's primary concern and once with a cross-cutting quality/standards query — and merge the results by rule id, topic results first. An empty rules list is a valid result (no relevant rules), not an error.

query.description:
Structured three-line query mirroring the rule embedding format:
Name: <concise 5-10 word title of the rule this task would trigger>
Category: <one of: Security, Correctness, Quality, Reliability, Performance, Testability, Compliance, Accessibility, Observability, Architecture>
Content: <1-2 sentences describing what should be checked or enforced; mention the tech stack when known>
Do NOT pass keyword lists or flat sentences — they retrieve poorly.

top_k.description: Optional max number of rules to return (1-50, default 10).

scopes.description: Optional repository scope paths to narrow results, e.g. '/owner/repo/' or '/owner/repo/modules/<name>/'. Omit entirely for org-wide search.

tools.name: rules-set-scope
tools.description: REPLACE the repository scope paths of one or more rules by id (no merge — the supplied scopes become each rule's full list; an empty list means the universal scope '/'). Requires admin permission. Confirm with the user before calling; set dry_run=true first to preview how many rules would change. Returns matched/succeeded counts plus per-id failures.

rule_ids.description: Id(s) of the rules to change (ruleId from search/list) — a single integer or a non-empty array of integers. At least one.

scopes.description: The NEW full list of scope paths for every selected rule (replaces the current scopes, no merge). An empty list sets the universal scope '/'.

dry_run.description: Preview only: report how many rules would change without changing anything. Default false.

tools.name: rules-set-state
tools.description: Activate or deactivate one or more rules by id in a single atomic call. Requires admin permission. Confirm with the user before calling; set dry_run=true first to preview how many rules would change. Returns matched/succeeded counts plus per-id failures.

rule_ids.description: Id(s) of the rules to change (ruleId from search/list) — a single integer or a non-empty array of integers. At least one.

state.description: Target state for every selected rule.

dry_run.description: Preview only: report how many rules would change without changing anything. Default false.

tools.name: rules-update
tools.description: Update an existing rule by id: supply only the fields to change — the tool fetches the current rule and merges (read-modify-write; a concurrent edit between fetch and save is overwritten). Setting state also lives here (pending/active/inactive); prefer rules-set-state for pure state changes across multiple rules. Requires admin permission. Confirm the exact change with the user before calling. Returns the updated rule.

rule_id.description: Id of the rule to update (ruleId from search/list).

scopes.description: New repository scope paths for the rule (replaces the current list, max 25). Omit to leave the existing scopes unchanged; pass [] for the universal scope '/'.

state.description: New lifecycle state. 'pending' turns the rule back into a suggestion.
